$comment: DRAFT ledger for issue #60, one director only (Ingmar Bergman). Same schema as essential10-example.json (schemaVersion 1) with additive fields: format, tmdbYear, sightAndSound2022, rt.reason, rt.alternateCut. Not approved, not for app use until the owner signs off the method and the score-display licensing decision.
methodSummary: Owner decision 2026-11-13: films are ranked by IMDb and Rotten Tomatoes scores. Each film is ranked within this list by IMDb rating and by Tomatometer (ties share the average rank); the two ranks are averaged (ranks, never the raw scores); ties are broken by higher IMDb rating, then more IMDb votes. A Tomatometer with fewer than 10 reviews or no value is ignored and that film is ranked by IMDb alone (flagged rtUsed:false). The film selection is unchanged from the editorial research list; editorialRank keeps the earlier order. Scores are read online and dated, never estimated.

imdb.source: IMDb non-commercial dataset title.ratings.tsv.gz (averageRating, numVotes), matched on IMDb title id; title ids found through title.crew.tsv.gz (director nconst) and cross-checked against TMDB by title, year and runtime
imdb.note: Live IMDb title pages were attempted first and did not return a usable page to an automated request (an empty response, not a human-readable page), so ratings come from the official daily dataset instead; this is the same fallback as the Kurosawa example. The dataset licence is personal / non-commercial use only; see licensing caveats in ESSENTIAL_10_EXAMPLE.md.

rt.source: Rotten Tomatoes film page, critics Tomatometer (scorePercent) and critic review count (reviewCount) read from the page's embedded data
rt.note: Read directly from each film's rottentomatoes.com page with a command-line fetch, one request per page. Percentages and counts are live and change; treat as a dated snapshot. Where a page shows fewer than about 5 reviews no Tomatometer is published and the value is null.

sightAndSound.source: BFI, The Greatest Films of All Time (2022 Sight and Sound poll), positions as listed on the page
sightAndSound.note: The page text was read in two halves; ranks 49-50 and the very bottom of the list were not visible in the extracted text. A film shown without a position was not seen in the portions read; that is not proof it is absent. '=' marks a tie. The page does not state 'critics' poll' in the extracted text, so the figure is labelled 'the 2022 Sight and Sound poll'.

films.title: Fanny and Alexander
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Writer). TMDB 5961 is the 188-minute theatrical version; the five-hour television version is a separate TMDB entry (TV 33153) and was not used.
films.rationale: A late summation: a child's view of a wealthy theatrical family and a cruel stepfather, with 100% on RT and one of his three Foreign Language Oscar winners.

films.title: The Seventh Seal
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Author, Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: A knight plays chess with Death across a plague-ridden Sweden; its images became shorthand for art-house cinema, and it leads this list on IMDb (8.1 from 219,144 votes) and RT review count (71).

films.title: Wild Strawberries
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: An old professor's road trip through memory and dream, carried by Victor Sjostrom; the humane counterweight to the austerity of the early canon.

films.title: Scenes from a Marriage
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Writer). Theatrical (169 minute) cut of a six-part television series (TMDB TV 65170, 1973; IMDb tt0070644, 8.5 from 17,954 votes). The film version is ranked here; TMDB, IMDb and RT all list it as a separate film entry. Flagged as a television-origin work.

rt.rtYearNote: RT page shows 1973 and a 2h 48m runtime, matching the theatrical cut.

films.rationale: The disintegration of a marriage in close two-handed scenes, with an IMDb rating of 8.3; ranked low because of its television origin and the thin sample for this cut (10,783 votes, 23 RT reviews).

films.title: Through a Glass Darkly
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: A four-person chamber drama on a Baltic island that opened the faith trilogy and won the Foreign Language Oscar; 100% on RT from 27 reviews.

films.title: Smiles of a Summer Night
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: The comedy of manners that first brought him international attention and later became the basis of the musical A Little Night Music; shows the range of the filmography.

films.title: Cries and Whispers
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: Three sisters and a maid in a house drenched in red, with Sven Nykvist's colour photography the film's argument; its Oscar was for cinematography.

films.title: Autumn Sonata
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: Ingrid Bergman and Liv Ullmann in a long mother-daughter reckoning, the only film to unite Ingrid Bergman with Ingmar Bergman; the closest call over Winter Light, Shame and Hour of the Wolf.

films.title: Persona
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay, Story).
films.rationale: Two women's identities blur until the film itself seems to tear and burn; the most formally radical film he made and the highest-placed Bergman in the 2022 Sight and Sound poll (18th).

films.title: The Virgin Spring
films.rationale: A medieval ballad of crime and revenge told with stark austerity; another of his three Foreign Language Oscar winners and 8.0 on IMDb.

nearMisses.title: Winter Light
nearMisses.reason: Completes the faith trilogy with Through a Glass Darkly; IMDb 8.0 but RT 80% from 25 reviews, below Autumn Sonata on the critic line.

nearMisses.title: Shame
nearMisses.reason: Strong war drama, but RT 68% from 25 reviews.

nearMisses.title: Hour of the Wolf
nearMisses.reason: Distinct horror turn; overlaps Persona's psychological ground.

nearMisses.title: Summer with Monika
nearMisses.reason: Influential on the French New Wave but not stronger than the ten; RT page not read.

nearMisses.title: Sawdust and Tinsel
nearMisses.reason: Important early work; only 11 RT reviews.

nearMisses.title: The Silence
nearMisses.reason: Completes the faith trilogy; not selected over the ten.

unverified: Scenes from a Marriage exists as a TV series and a theatrical cut; the film entries (TMDB 133919, IMDb tt6725014, RT /m/scenes_from_a_marriage, 2h 48m) were used throughout. The IMDb series entry (tt0070644) has a higher vote count and rating (8.5 from 17,954); do not mix the two.
Fanny and Alexander has a theatrical cut (used) and a five-hour TV cut (TMDB TV 33153); the RT page shows a 3h 8m runtime, matching the theatrical cut.
RT pages for The Virgin Spring (shown as 1959) and others show US release years; the ledger uses the original release year.
RT pages for Summer with Monika, The Silence and The Magician were not read because those films are not in the ten; they were not needed for the decision.
Runtime gaps between TMDB and IMDb: Autumn Sonata 93 vs 99 minutes, Cries and Whispers 95 vs 92; both are the same film (single entry each).
